label: Pleomorphic_Adenoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Most common salivary gland tumor in both children and adults, most often parotid
- Biphasic/“triphasic” tumor with ductal epithelial and myoepithelial cells in distinctive stroma
- Encapsulated in major glands, circumscribed but not encapsulated in minor glands
- PLAG1 and/or HMGA2 rearrangement present in ~70% (molecular hallmark)
- Malignant transformation (carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma) risk ≈5%
- Recurrence risk increased with incomplete removal

## Terminology

- “Benign mixed tumor” is an accepted synonym
- “Mixed tumor” often used interchangeably
- “Congenital pleomorphic adenoma” is not recommended—use “salivary gland anlage tumor” ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Salivary_Gland_Anlage_Tumour.html))

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Biphasic (traditionally “triphasic”) architecture with both ductal epithelial and myoepithelial cell populations ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
  - Encapsulated in parotid/major salivary glands; circumscribed (not encapsulated) in minor glands
  - Classic stroma: myxoid, chondromyxoid, or hyalinized areas
  - PLAG1 or HMGA2 rearrangement (~70%) ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- **Desirable:**
  - Metaplastic changes: adipose, osseous, squamous, mucinous, sebaceous (seen but not required)
  - Tyrosine crystals (rare, not diagnostic)
  - Bland cytology, low mitotic activity
  - Absence of necrosis or overt invasion

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- PLAG1 (8q12) or HMGA2 (12q14-15) gene fusions in ~70% ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Prior radiation increases risk ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Hamartomatous/heterotopic origins suggested for rare congenital cases ([Hn Gnepp](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Gnepp.pdf#page=448))

## Clinical Issues

- **Epidemiology:** Most common salivary gland neoplasm (54–76% of all; all ages) ([Hn Thompson](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Thompson.pdf#page=294))
- **Sites:** Parotid (most), minor salivary glands (palate), submandibular, sublingual, lacrimal gland ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- **Presentation:** Slow-growing, painless, well-circumscribed mass
- **Natural course:** Recurrences possible if not completely excised (15–25% with enucleation); transformation risk ~5%
- **Treatment:** Complete surgical excision with negative margins ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)); radiation considered for unresectable recurrences
- **Prognosis:** Excellent with complete excision

## Macroscopic

- Well-demarcated, bosselated, solid, gray-white myxoid mass
- Encapsulated in major glands, circumscribed in minor glands
- Cut surface rubbery, solid/cystic, may appear partly myxoid
- Recurrent: multiple myxoid to fibrotic nodules (“shotgun bullet” appearance)
- Bosselated surface with tongue-like pseudopods
- ![Firm, whitish tan, well-encapsulated mass, submandibular gland](https://pathology-hub-v04-vorn5q2kga-uc.a.run.app/figures/textbook?u=Z3M6Ly9wYXRob2xvZ3lfaHViLzAxX3N0YWdlZC90ZXh0Ym9va3MvYXNzZXRzL2ZpZ3VyZV9pbWFnZXMvaG5fZ25lcHAvaG5fZ25lcHBfcDA0NzJfZmlnMDFfZmlnXzZfMTIuanBlZw&exp=1784974064&sig=862cb9b3f69924512f27a91e92f9adf819d16e56f72e05ed235e2bf6dcbb3d08)

## Microscopic

- Biphasic/triphasic: ductal epithelial cells, myoepithelial cells, and variable stroma ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Ducts/tubules lined by epithelial cells, surrounded by myoepithelial cells (spindle, plasmacytoid, clear, etc.)
- Stroma: myxoid, chondromyxoid, hyalinized, or fibrous; may have metaplastic adipose, bone, squamous areas
- Variants: stroma-rich (“myxoid”), cellular (“myoepithelial-predominant”), classic mixed—stroma-rich type more prone to recurrence
- Tyrosine crystals (eosinophilic floret-shaped, rare)
- No necrosis or significant mitotic activity in benign cases
- Encapsulated or circumscribed depending on site ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=979))
- ![Admixture of epithelial, myoepithelial cells, and chondromyxoid stroma](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_atlas/hn_atlas_p1187_fig01_fig_21_4.jpeg)

## Cytology

- Smears show mixture of myoepithelial and ductal cells, metachromatic feathery/fibrillary, magenta stroma on Romanowsky stains, gray-green chondromyxoid stroma on Pap stain ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Cohesive groups of epithelial cells with bland nuclei, and myoepithelial cells (spindle, plasmacytoid, epithelioid)
- Background is typically filled with bluish-purple, mucoid or fibromyxoid stromal fragments
- Risk of malignancy is <5% when classic features present ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsneoplasmbenign.html))
- Image:
  - ![Fine needle aspiration, triphasic cells and stroma](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_atlas/hn_atlas_p0978_fig02_fig_20_5.jpeg)

## Ancillary Tests

- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - Ductal (epithelial) cells: positive for cytokeratins (AE1/AE3, CAM5.2, CK7)
  - Myoepithelial cells: S100, GFAP, SOX10, smooth muscle actin, calponin, p40, p63
  - PLAG1 and HMGA2: surrogate IHC for gene fusions ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)); nuclear PLAG1 supports Dx ([Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Atlas.pdf#page=979))
  - Vimentin: positive in myoepithelial component
  - Negative for melanoma markers (MelanA, HMB45)
- **Molecular:** PLAG1 or HMGA2 fusions present in ~70% ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- **Special stains:** Stroma is magenta (Romanowsky) or gray-green (Pap)

## Radiology

- Well-defined, bosselated border
- Hyperintense on T2-weighted MRI ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))

## Differential Diagnosis

| Feature                      | Pleomorphic Adenoma                                                    | Carcinoma ex Pleomorphic Adenoma                      | Myoepithelioma/Myoepithelial Carcinoma           | Basal Cell Adenoma                                                 | Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma                      | Polymorphous Adenocarcinoma              | Epithelial-Myoepithelial Carcinoma      |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Ductal epithelial cells      | Present, part of tri/biphasic mix                                     | Present; plus malignant cytology and invasion         | Scant or absent (monomorphic myoepithelial cells)| Non-invasive, biphasic basaloid morphology; peripheral palisading  | Tubular/cribriform, perineural invasion      | Uniform ductal/glandular, infiltrative    | Dual cell layers, clear cells, hyaline    |
| Myoepithelial cells          | Varied: spindled, plasmacytoid, clear, etc.                           | May be overtaken by malignant component               | Exclusively myoepithelial (except rare ducts)    | Basaloid and luminal cells, minimal myxoid stroma                  | Variable, less prominent                     | Limited or absent                         | Myoepithelial outer layer, also present   |
| Stroma                       | Myxoid, chondromyxoid, hyalinized; variable                           | May be hyalinized; can show invasion                 | Minimal, usually not overt myxoid/chondroid      | Variable collagenous, little to no myxoid stroma                   | Hyalinized/cribriform (“Swiss cheese” holes) | Fibrous/hyalinized, Indian file pattern   | Hyalinized/extracellular basement membrane|
| Capsule/Border               | Encapsulated (parotid); circumscribed (minor)                         | Invasion beyond capsule, perineural/LV invasion      | Well-defined, non-invasive                       | Well-circumscribed, non-invasive                                   | Infiltrative, perineural invasion            | Infiltrative, lobular                     | Infiltrative                              |
| Ductal structures            | Readily present                                                       | Readily present                                      | Rare or absent                                   | Rare ductal structures                                            | Tubular/cribriform, sometimes with ducts     | Ductal/glandular only                     | Ductal with clear myoepithelial rim       |
| Cytology                     | Bland, low mitoses, no frank necrosis                                 | Marked pleomorphism, necrosis, increased mitoses     | Monomorphic, bland, rare mitoses                 | Bland, dual pop. cells, nuclear β-catenin                          | Small angulated cells, hyperchromatic         | Low cytologic atypia                       | Clear cells, double layers, hyaline core   |

- Adenoid cystic carcinoma: cribriform (“Swiss cheese”), tubular or solid growth, perineural invasion, lacks true triphasic pattern ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- Polymorphous adenocarcinoma: uniformly bland cells, lobular/“Indian file” pattern, fibrous stroma, lacks tri/biphasic mix ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
- Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma: tubular/ductal structures lined by inner epithelial and outer clear myoepithelial cells, hyalinized basement membrane material ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Basal cell adenoma: non-invasive, biphasic basaloid/luminal cells; minimal/absent myxoid stroma, peripheral palisading; lacks triphasic architecture ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Basal_Cell_Adenoma.html))
- Myoepithelioma (including myoepithelial carcinoma): exclusively myoepithelial cells, rare or absent ductal structures, lacks classic stromal features of PA; monomorphic histology separates from PA ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Salivary_Gland_Myoepithelioma.html)), ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma: frank evidence of malignancy—nuclear pleomorphism, necrosis, mitoses, invasion; can retain PLAG1/HMGA2 fusion ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))

## Prognostic Factors

- Local recurrence risk: 15–25% with enucleation; reduced with negative surgical margins ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
- Multiple recurrences, submandibular site, advanced age, larger tumor, radiation exposure, prominent hyalinization increase malignant transformation risk
- Stroma-rich (“myxoid”) variants more prone to recurrence ([Hn Thompson](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Thompson.pdf#page=294))
- Malignant transformation risk ~5%; can recur up to 50 years after initial excision

## Illustrative Cases

- 6-year-old girl (parotid), 28-year-old man (submandibular), 54-year-old man (upper lip), 84-year-old man (parotid), rare metastasizing PA with recurrent PLAG1/HMGA2 gene fusion ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))

cards.title: Salivary gland myoepithelioma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Salivary gland myoepithelioma Section: differential_diagnosis The well-defined borders of the tumour and the lack of invasive growth distinguish ME from myoepithelial carcinoma. The characteristic basaloid biphasic pattern, peripheral palisading, and minimal to absent myxoid stroma of basal cell adenoma help to separate it from ME. Monomorphic histology and rare or absent ductal structures in ME separate it from pleomorphic adenoma. Distinguishing from soft tissue ME may be difficult, given the overlapping histological features and the presence of PLAG1 gene rearrangements in both.

cards.excerpt:
Most commonly affected site is the parotid gland (84% of cases)
May also occur in other major salivary glands (submandibular and sublingual glands), lacrimal gland and minor salivary glands of upper aerodigestive tract (El-Naggar: WHO Classification of Head and Neck Tumours, 4th Edition, 2017)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Benign metastasizing mixed tumors
cards.excerpt:
Rare, controversial clinical entity with late metastasis (6 - 52 years) after tumor excision
Metastatic sites include bone, CNS, kidney, liver, lung, lymph nodes, maxilla, pharynx, skin, sphenoid sinus

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Benign tumor: surgical resection with negative margin is considered curative
cards.excerpt:
Enucleation is associated with 15 - 25% risk of local recurrence
Recurrences are usually within 18 months but can be up to 50 years later (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2008;132:1445)
Risk of malignant transformation is ~5%
Risk factors for malignant transformation: multiple recurrences, submandibular location, older age, larger size, prominent hyalinization, increased mitotic rate (if present, sample tumor more thoroughly), radiation exposure

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Typically has 3 components
cards.excerpt:
Epithelial (ductal) component forming the inner layer of cysts and tubules
Myoepithelial cells as the outer layer of cysts and tubules and scattered within the myxoid stroma
Cytology of myoepithelial cells can be plasmacytoid, spindled, epithelioid, clear or stellate shaped

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Stromal component is typically myxoid, chondroid or myxochondroid
cards.excerpt:
It can also be hyalinized or fibrotic
Metaplastic changes may be seen, e.g. adipose metaplasia, osseous metaplasia, squamous metaplasia (sometimes with keratinization), sebaceous metaplasia and mucinous metaplasia
Intravascular permeation has been reported in a small percentage of cases and does not increase the risk of recurrence or distant metastasis
It is proposed to be a phenomenon associated with surgical manipulation (Am J Surg Pathol 2012;36:1674)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Typical feature is its unique fibrillary stroma
cards.excerpt:
Mixture of myoepithelial cells, ductal cells and extracellular stroma
Myoepithelial cells are usually the predominant cell type with various cytomorphology, including round, polygonal, plasmacytoid, spindle, etc.
Ductal cells show bland cytologic features with organized honeycombing or ductal arrangement
Extracellular matrix shows characteristic feathery / fibrillary borders and bright magenta color on Romanowsky type stain and gray-green chondromyxoid features on Papanicolaou stain
Cytology imagesContributed by Bin Xu, M.D., Ph.D., Jen-Fan Hang, M.D. and Shuanzeng (Sam) Wei, M.D., Ph.D.

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Goblet cell
cards.excerpt:
Positive stains
Ductal (epithelial) cells are typically positive for cytokeratins (e.g. AE1 / AE3, CAM5.2 and CK7)
Myoepithelial cells are positive for GFAP, S100, SOX10, actin - alpha smooth muscle, calponin, p40 and p63
PLAG1 and HMGA2 can be used as surrogate immunohistochemical markers for underlying PLAG1 or HMGA2 fusion (Histopathology 2018;72:285, Histopathology 2017;71:511)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Essential features
cards.heading: Essential features
cards.text_excerpt:
Primary pulmonary pleomorphic adenoma is a very rare benign tumor that tends to arise in the large airways
Tumors tend to show small, branching, double layered ductules rather than ducts and less cartilaginous stroma as compared to pleomorphic adenomas arising in the salivary gland
Keratin and vimentin staining of the epithelial component supports diagnosis of primary pulmonary tumor as opposed to only keratin staining in salivary gland tumors (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2003;127:621)
Prognosis is generally good, but cases of carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenom have been reported
